output.text: What if a time traveler prevents their own birth? The paradox unfolds: to exist, they must travel back; to travel back, they must exist. Yet their intervention erases the condition of their existence. Causality collapses—cause and effect negate each other. No origin, no destination. The traveler becomes a ghost in their own past, a memory that never was. This is not mere contradiction; it is ontological self-annihilation. The universe may reject such a loop—time could fold inward, sealing the breach. Or perhaps the paradox is the universe’s silent correction: some doors, once opened, must remain closed.
